backstory: The single do-everything server of a fictional 20-person outdoor-gear retailer: company website, mail, file sharing, and the store database all live on one box — because that is what small businesses actually do.
deception_notes: Why these six: SSH (22) for remote admin, HTTP (80) for the company website, SMTP (25) for company mail, FTP (21) for file sharing with vendors, MySQL (3306) backing the website, RDP (3389) for Windows admin — one coherent story of a small shop running everything on a single machine. Why the rest are LEFT OUT: telnet screams trap on any modern box (nobody deploys new telnet); redis/elasticsearch/mongodb are exotic for a 20-person retailer and would make a scanner suspicious; docker smells like a dev-ops shop, not a retailer; vnc is redundant next to RDP; postgres/mssql are redundant next to MySQL — one database is the believable choice. Six believable doors beat fourteen random ones: a scanner that sees every port open knows it is looking at a honeypot.
name: Small Business Server
